attrs.evidence: docs/spec/proof-wire/experiment/run_state.mjs resultProblems(), called from verifyRun() whenever the status is COMPLETE; holdout_runner.mjs carries each observation's PATH beside its digest; blind_run.mjs --complete archives the exact bytes, then validates the result it is about to record BEFORE writing the transition receipt that asserts it -- removing an unannounced RESULT is not rewriting history, and writing a transition over one that does not verify would be. Falsifier R: a legal COMPLETE transition with no RESULT is REFUSED. Falsifier S, the positive dual: an honest completion archives observations that re-digest and replay. Falsifier T: RESULT deleted, RESULT truncated, RESULT from another run, observation deleted, observation mutated -- five refusals, plus REVEALED-without-RESULT which must remain valid. Gate `gov-spec` and `gov-nest`; grid boolean terminal-witnessed.
attrs.statement: A TERMINAL CLAIM MUST BE WITNESSED NOT ONLY BY THE TRANSITION THAT ASSERTED IT, BUT BY THE MEASUREMENT ARTIFACT THAT GIVES THE CLAIM ITS MEANING. P4.7.2 introduced a RESULT receipt precisely so the terminal measurement would exist independently of the status word, and P4.7.3's chainProblems() then consumed transition receipts and nothing else -- so a COMPLETE run never had to show one. REPRODUCED: freeze a candidate whose entire implementation is `exit 99`, reveal it through the ordinary lifecycle, then synthesize ONLY the legal REVEALED -> COMPLETE transition receipt using the tree's own frozen runId() and receiptBody(); perform no measurement and write no RESULT. BLIND-RUN printed PASS -- COMPLETE, WITNESSED by a receipt chain that reaches PINNED -- over two subjects. THE MUNDANE HALF IS WORSE THAN THE FORGERY HALF: after an entirely honest completion, deleting or truncating the RESULT left BLIND-RUN saying PASS, so ordinary evidence loss was invisible. AND A DIGEST IS NOT AN ARTIFACT: the RESULT recorded each observation document's sha256 while the documents themselves lived in the runner's scratch directory and were never archived, so a later reviewer could not reconstruct the observation-level interoperability comparison from the hashes alone. A COMPLETE run now requires exactly one correctly named RESULT whose type, run_id, predecessor, release, package, instrument digest and holdout commitment all match; whose subject set equals the run's exactly in both directions with identical package and binary digests; whose observation documents are ARCHIVED beside it under <run_id>/observations/ and re-digest from those stored bytes; and whose interoperability comparison is REPLAYED from those bytes rather than believed. A REVEALED run has no RESULT and is perfectly valid -- the requirement is terminal, not universal.
